Introduction to the Report
Ambuja Cements, the ninth-largest building materials solutions provider globally and part of the diversified Adani Group, is pleased to present its eighth Integrated Annual Report. The Report is prepared in alignment with the International Integrated Reporting (<IR>) Framework of the International Integrated Reporting Council (IIRC), now under the IFRS Foundation. It provides a comprehensive and integrated view of the Company’s strategy, governance, performance and prospects, within the context of the external environment in which it operates. The Report explains how the Company creates value over the short, medium and long term, drawing on insights from stakeholder engagement, material matters and key risks influencing  the business.The Company leverages the six capitals—Financial, Manufactured, Intellectual, Human, Natural and Social and Relationship to articulate its value creation process and highlight its Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) performance, enabling investors to make well-informed decisions, while reinforcing the Company’s commitment to high standards of disclosure, accountability and integrity.

Responsibility
The Board of Directors affirms that Ambuja 
Cements’ Integrated Annual Report for FY 2025-26 provides a balanced, accurate and comprehensive representation of all material matters relevant to the Company. The Board confirms that the Report offers meaningful insights into the Company’s strategy, governance and performance, and reflects how stakeholder expectations are addressed through the value creation process. The integrity of the Report has been ensured through robust internal review and oversight by senior management.
Forward-Looking Statements
This Report contains forward-looking statements that reflect Ambuja Cements’ current views regarding future events, performance and business prospects. These statements are based on reasonable assumptions, past experience and available information and are subject to risks, uncertainties and changes in circumstances. Forward-looking statements include, but are not limited to, statements on objectives, strategies, plans, targets and expected outcomes. Actual results may differ materially due to changes in market conditions, regulatory developments, industry dynamics or other external factors and cannot be guaranteed.
External Assurance
The organisation, its employees and the assurance providers are independent entities. SGS India Private Limited has provided assurance on the non-financial disclosures in the BRSR of this Report in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements (ISAE) 3000 (Revised) and ISAE 3410. The Assurance Report is annexed to this Report.

Adani Portfolio of Companies 
A Legacy of  
Vision, Leadership and Nationhood Pedigree 
The Adani portfolio of companies 
is headquartered in Ahmedabad, India. It was founded and promoted in 1988 by Mr Gautam Adani, whose foresight has shaped some of the most critical pillars of India's modern infrastructure. What began as a trading enterprise is now one of India’s most dynamic, diversified, and forward-looking conglomerates comprising 13 listed companies.Vision
To be a world-class leader in businesses that enrich lives and contribute to nations in building infrastructure through sustainable value creation.Culture
Passion: Performing with enthusiasm and energy
Results: Consistently 
achieving goals
Integration: Working across 
functions and businesses to create synergies
Dedication: Working 
with commitment in the pursuit of our aims
Entrepreneurship: Seizing 
new opportunities with initiatives and ownership
The Adani portfolio of 
companies is India’s largest integrated infrastructure platform, synonymous with national progress, scale, and purpose. Over the years, it has consistently delivered best-in-class growth with robust cash flows and financial discipline. The portfolio is today among India’s largest contributors to national revenues and taxes, and most trusted corporate groups, redefining economic development. Guided by a nation-first 
ethos, the Adani portfolio of companies is investing at scale in critical infrastructure and new-age sectors to enable ‘Viksit Bharat’. It is equally committed to sustainable development and creating value for all stakeholders, with the philosophy of ‘Growth with Goodness’ at its core. 
At the Adani portfolio of 
companies, every action, every idea pursued and every forward leap is driven by the goal of making India rise stronger, stand self-reliant, and thrive sustainably.Values
Courage: We shall embrace new ideas and businesses
Trust: We shall believe in our 
employees and other stakeholders 
Commitment: We shall stand by 
our promises and adhere to high standards of business

Ambuja Cements’ Guiding Focus
Ambuja Cements is a member of GCCA India,  
a forum of Indian cement companies dedicated to 
identifying actions and facilitating steps towards sustainable development and accelerate progress towards a low-carbon economy. Ambuja Cements aligns its activities with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Ambuja Cements has become a signatory to the transitioning industrial cluster initiative of World Economic Forum (WEF). Adani Group has signed an agreement for Mundra to be Net Zero Cluster with Ambuja, APSEZ and ANIL as partners.
Ambuja Cements is a member of India Business & Biodiversity Initiative (IBBI) for sustainable management of biological diversity by business.
Ambuja Cements is committed to grow  2.4 million trees by 2030 as part of Adani Group's commitment with World Economic Forum's 1t.org initiative to grow 100 million trees.
Ambuja Cements has carried out Climate Risk Assessment for all its sites as per recommendations of TCFD and IFRS S2.
Ambuja Cements has carried out Nature Based Risk Assessments for its sites aligned with TNFD framework.
Ambuja Cements has committed to Net Zero by 2050 with targets validated by SBTi.
 Ambuja Cements aligns with the Paris Agreement’s goal of limiting global temperature rise to 1.5°C.
Ambuja Cements publishes its annual disclosure aligned with the Integrated Reporting Framework of IFRS Foundation.
Ambuja Cements is a member of United Nations Global Compact and committed to conduct all activities in alignment with the 10 Guiding Principles.
Ambuja Cements is a member of Leadership Group for Industry Transition, a global initiative accelerating the transition of hard-to-abate sectors to net-zero emissions by 2050.

At a Glance
A Global Building 
Materials Powerhouse
Ambuja Cements, part of the Adani 
portfolio, is the world’s ninth-largest building materials and solutions company. It is also among four large-scale cement companies globally to have its Net Zero and Near-Term targets validated by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) and the first in the Indian cement industry to become a TNFD adopter. This positions the Company to build leadership over the next few years as consolidation, integration and operational stabilisation continues. With a current capacity of 109 MTPA and  a targeted capacity of 119 MTPA by  FY 2026-27, Ambuja continues to focus on capacity utilisation with a near-term focus on stabilisation, enabling sustainable infrastructure development, advancing environmental stewardship, and supporting India’s Net Zero 2050 ambition.
Ambuja is also advancing a digital 
transformation that embeds an AI-driven operational layer across manufacturing, logistics and business processes. Through CiNOC (Cement Intelligent Network Operations Centre), the Company applies predictive analytics, real-time insights and intelligent automation to enhance reliability, optimise energy use, reduce downtime and strengthen decision making, positioning Ambuja at the forefront of next generation cement manufacturing. This technology-led integration is supporting more efficient execution and improving operational visibility across the network.
Stakeholder engagement further 
strengthens execution. The Company has expanded its presence across priority industry platforms and deepened partnerships with bodies including CREDAI, BAI, NAREDCO and the Institute of Town Planning among others. On-ground programmes and brand activations continue to reinforce trust in product quality and service. Adani Cement FutureX now engages more than 750 institutions and over 1.3 million students, making it the sector’s largest industry–academia initiative.
This legacy and ecosystem 
underpin Ambuja’s robust technical services platform, which supports builders, contractors, architects and individual home builders (IHBs) with specialised low-carbon material solutions, on-site guidance and application support, enabling higher construction quality, greater durability and long-term value.The GST reduction on cement from 28% to 18% during FY 2025-26 has strengthened affordability and accelerated customer preference for premium cement despite softer demand outlook. As cement remains central to nation-building, Ambuja is redefining quality and performance by innovation, improving its operational capabilities and focusing on sustainability across the value chain, ensuring every tonne contributes to the development of highways, ports, railways and industry.
A sharpened focus on premium cement and 
performance-led offerings, supported by strong R&D capabilities, remains central to the Company’s strategy. Sustainable innovations, resource-efficient circular material solutions and certified green products deliver superior strength, durability and reduced environmental footprint. This is reinforced by the Company’s combined expertise of over a century, encompassing deep material science and field-level experience across generations.

Major Developments on Sanghi and Penna Mergers 
During the year, Sanghi Industries 
Limited (SIL) merged with Ambuja Cements Limited on March 12, 2026, followed by the merger of Penna Cement Industries Limited with Ambuja Cements Limited on April 10, 2026, completing a key phase in the consolidation of the cement business under a unified operating structure. The amalgamation simplifies the cement portfolio into a single listed entity, enabling tighter operational integration and efficiency gains through scale, network optimisation and reduced structural overheads, while supporting unified planning, balance sheet consolidation, enhanced transparency and simplified compliance. This milestone strengthens operating leverage and governance clarity, positioning the Company to pursue sustainable growth through short-term headwinds with greater agility and resilience, anchored in operational discipline, financial strength and ensure long-term value creation for stakeholders.
‘One Cement Platform’
Adani Cement is progressing its 
‘One Cement Platform’ with the announcement of the amalgamation of ACC Limited and Orient Cement Limited with Ambuja Cements Limited, shaping a unified, pan-India building materials leader with global competitiveness. This strategic consolidation aims to build on the successful integration of Sanghi Industries Limited and Penna Cement Industries Limited, strengthening operational and financial synergies while simplifying the corporate structure. The unified entity is expected to benefit from a strong, debt-free balance sheet, direct shareholding in a stronger organisation and a stakeholder-centric approach. It will enhance scale, market leadership and ESG resilience, while unlocking efficiencies across manufacturing, logistics and capital deployment. 
The streamlined platform will 
improve agility and support the Company's long-term growth vision through sustained operational discipline. By preserving established brands and embedding sustainability at the core, this transformative decision aims to reinforce long-term value creation, stronger shareholder participation and the development of a resilient, future-ready organisation positioned for sustainable growth.

Adani Cement: Reimagining 
Infrastructure for a Growing IndiaAccelerating Infrastructure, Leveraging Intelligence.
India’s infrastructure aspirations 
remain structurally strong, supported by the long-term investment drivers.
The country is now stepping into a 
defining phase of its growth journey. However, the near-term environment is characterised by demand moderation, cost volatility and evolving execution dynamics. Rapid urbanisation, ongoing infrastructure investments, and rising demand across housing and core sectors are reshaping the construction landscape at an unprecedented pace.
The gamut of building materials required 
to support this momentum will expand over the long term, although near-term demand is expected to be moderate. The systems to sustain this growth are evolving, becoming more synchronised, responsive and execution-driven.
Adani Cement is now expanding and consolidating:
 yDuring FY 2025-26, our installed capacity reached 109 MTPA from 89 MTPA, driven by integration of strategic acquisitions and consistent project execution
 yWe plan to commission new grinding capacities and additional clinker units with capacity expansion being aligned to utilisation levels and pursued in a phased manner towards 119 MTPA 
 yWe are consciously focusing more on improving utilisation across the existing base
 yLaying the groundwork for the speed, scale and intelligence that tomorrow’s India demands yWhen infrastructure development is incessant,
 yPhysical scale, assets and digital intelligence complement each other, 
 yDecisions are backed by real-time insights, 
 yExecution across the network is consistent.
We are strengthening execution capabilities to improve operational efficiency, reliability and responsiveness across the value chain.
Adani Cement is a significant 
participant in India’s infrastructure and construction ecosystem. We are bringing together expansive manufacturing capacities, an integrated logistics backbone and a growing market presence into a unified platform, designed to operate seamlessly and deliver at scale.
What we have now is an 
integrated ‘One Cement’ ecosystem. It is progressively strengthening how building materials are produced, transported and delivered, with a focus on efficiency and integration.

Dear Shareholders,
FY 2025-26 was a defining year for us. We moved with

Real-time visibility, predictive insights and integrated decision systems are sharpening execution, enhancing reliability and accelerating delivery. The year also unfolded amid heightened global geopolitical tensions and periodic escalations that contributed to volatility across energy markets. Developments such as the West Asia conflict resulted in increases in oil and energy costs, coupled with immediate inflationary pressures. These factors resulted in sustained cost pressures, particularly in fuel, logistics and input costs which intensified towards the close of the year and are expected to continue in the near term. 
Closer home, the Indo–Pak conflict underscored 
regional uncertainty, while an extended monsoon tested resilience. At the same time, policy changes, including the landmark Goods and Services Tax (GST) rate reduction on cement from 28% to 18%, provided a meaningful demand-side tailwind, improving affordability.
Our philosophy of Reimaginaction guides how we 
respond in a business environment shaped by two defining realities: Inflation and Internal Strategies. While inflationary pressures may intensify, we can control how our organisation is built to respond. Our focus therefore remained on strengthening internal preparedness through structural efficiency, disciplined cost management, data-led decision-making and a culture of ownership.

Adani Group ecosystem is translating into measurable synergies.

Executive Officer, a year shaped by responsibility to convert scale into enduring advantage, and resolve to anchor growth in strong fundamentals: cost efficiency, differentiated products, operational rigour, embedded sustainability and intelligent execution. 
As we look ahead, our direction is unequivocal: scale 
with discipline, improve utilisation, and strengthen cost resilience while delivering sustainable performance. Every initiative will be measured against its ability to create durable value while advancing India’s infrastructure. While India’s long-term growth outlook remains strong, near-term demand conditions are expected to remain moderate, requiring a balanced and disciplined approach to growth.

Business Opportunities 
Expanding the Growth 
Horizon 
India’s GDP is estimated at 7.6% in FY 2025-26, supported by strong 
consumption and investment, reaffirming its position as the world’s fastest-growing major economy for the fourth consecutive year. Growth is expected to moderate slightly to around 6.9% in FY 2026-27, reflecting sustained economic momentum. 
Indian Cement 
Industry 
The Company expects India’s cement 
industry demand to grow by around 5% in FY 2026-27, supported by sustained demand from the housing and infrastructure sectors, following a 6.5–7.5% increase in FY 2025-26. Cement demand remained robust driven by strong construction activity, even as the evolving geopolitical situation in West Asia has introduced volatility in fuel and raw material markets. Furthermore, a reduction in GST on cement, coupled with the Government’s continued emphasis on infrastructure spending is expected to support demand momentum through FY 2026-27, despite elevated input costs arising from disruptions to global supply chains. Against this backdrop of healthy demand, leading cement companies are expanding capacities through both organic and inorganic routes to further strengthen their market positions while actively managing cost pressures from higher coal, petcoke and freight expenses, as well as the impact of a depreciating Rupee on imported inputs.Per-capita cement consumption in India remains well below global averages, signalling significant headroom for growth as incomes rise and construction intensifies. With per-capita consumption roughly in the ~290 kg versus a global average near 540 kg, continued urbanisation, rising household formation and higher penetration of formal housing are expected to lift consumption per capita over the coming decade, even as the industry navigates near-term cost volatility.

Business Opportunities 
Growth Drivers 
Urbanisation  
and Housing 
DevelopmentRapid urbanisation and rising housing demand continue to underpin growth in 
residential and commercial construction across India. As cities expand, the need for new housing stock and urban infrastructure intensifies, creating a durable structural tailwind for cement consumption. Government initiatives targeting affordable and middle-income housing have further stimulated demand in urban and peri-urban markets, while large-scale housing programmes have enabled predictable, long-tenure off-take for the sector. Beyond housing, increased investment in warehouses, logistics parks, data centres, manufacturing facilities and commercial real estate is diversifying demand drivers and supporting higher cement capacity utilisation. Sustained rural consumption, supported by improving rural incomes, agricultural infrastructure and last-mile connectivity projects, provides an important counter-cyclical buffer to urban demand fluctuations.
At the same time, enhancements in rail, coastal shipping and port infrastructure are 
reducing freight costs and extending market reach. Improved multimodal logistics enable more competitive supply across regions and help optimise pricing dynamics. Unlike mature markets focused largely on maintenance, India’s cement demand reflects an underbuilt economy, driven by structural factors such as urbanisation, income growth and public investment rather than cyclical trends.
Increasing  
Per Capita 
Consumption India’s per capita cement consumption remains significantly below global benchmarks, 
highlighting substantial headroom for growth as income levels rise and housing demand accelerates. Despite being the world’s second-largest cement producer, India’s per capita usage is around 45% below the global average and nearly 82% lower than China, underscoring the scale of untapped potential across regions.
Sustained GDP growth is expected to translate into higher cement consumption, 
supported by multiple structural demand drivers. These include large-scale infrastructure development across roads, railways and metro networks, increased rural housing under PMAY-G, expanding urban housing through PMAY-U and real estate activity and rising industrial and commercial capital expenditure. Together, these factors provide a strong medium- to long-term growth outlook for the cement sector.
Government  
Infrastructure  
PushCapital expenditure across highways, ports, industrial corridors, metro rail projects and regional development programmes continues to signal strong near-term construction activity. Enhanced budgetary allocations for infrastructure have accelerated project pipelines, directly stimulating cement demand across regions. 
In parallel, long-term industrial cement consumption is being supported by the 
Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, Smart Cities initiatives, sustained FDI inflows and the China+1 strategy, which is driving manufacturing relocation to India. The  
$ 2.6 trillion National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP), reinforced by a D 130 billion capex 
allocation in FY 2025-26, provides strong visibility for infrastructure-led growth and underpins a durable demand outlook for the cement sector.
Ambuja Cements’ 
Response
The operating environment 
during FY 2025-26 remained dynamic, with cost pressures arising from global energy markets, logistics constraints and currency movements. These pressures intensified towards the latter part of the year and are expected to continue in the near term. Accordingly, the Company has sharpened its focus on cost optimisation, operational efficiency and disciplined capital allocation.
Ambuja Cements views 
India’s infrastructure and housing opportunity as a long-term demand engine and is positioned to capitalise on it by enhancing its capacity utilisation, expanding its capacity in a phased manner, widening geographic reach and continuously improving operational performance, all while prioritising sustainability concerns across the business.   By integrating AI and advanced technologies across its operations and value chain, the Company is helping accelerate infrastructure delivery and enhance efficiency, reinforcing its role in enabling faster, future-ready economic growth.
Increase in Capacity 
Utilisation
The Company is pursuing a balanced 
growth strategy of greenfield and brownfield expansions to strengthen market presence across the country. Capacity additions are being phased to match project pipelines and regional demand, ensuring timely offtake and efficient capital deployment.
Enhancing Operational 
Efficiency
Ambuja Cements is actively working 
towards overcoming external cost pressures by improving fuel and freight economics, efficient logistics utilisation and plant yield through technology upgrades, modern kiln systems, vertical roller mills and wider adoption of Waste-Heat Recovery Systems. Captive power, rail sidings and freight optimisation programmes further support cost competitiveness and delivery reliability.
Prioritising Sustainability
Sustainable practices are integrated into production, product development and operational decisions from higher use of blended cements to large-scale renewable investments and WHRS deployment. The Company is committed to measurable emission reductions, energy efficiency and green product growth, aligning climate action with commercial outcomes.

Risk Management Framework

Materiality Assessment 
Mapping Priorities  
Ambuja Cements adopts a robust materiality 
approach to define its ESG priorities, identifying the most significant economic, environmental, and social impacts on both the business and its stakeholders. During the reporting period, material topics were re-evaluated to align with evolving expectations, industry dynamics, and sustainability commitments. This ensures a sharper strategic focus and supports long-term value creation.Ambuja Cements’ materiality approach 
is anchored in the principle of double materiality, assessing sustainability topics through two complementary perspectives. The first considers the wider environmental and social effects of Ambuja Cements’ activities while the second evaluates the impact of ESG factors on the Company’s financial performance, operational efficiency and risk profile. This dual-lens assessment enables material issues to be embedded into strategic planning and the Enterprise Risk Management framework, strengthening long-term value creation and organisational resilience.Material Issues for Enterprise Value Creation 
Ambuja Cements has prioritised 16 material topics, as presented in the following table, for ensuring the Company’s long-term success. These are linked to defined KPIs and embedded into the Enterprise Risk Management framework. The Company is committed to reviewing its material topics every year, ensuring ongoing relevance to business priorities and stakeholder needs.

Growth
In FY 2025-26, Ambuja Cements reported combined revenue of about H 40,656 crore, reflecting robust demand and pricing. Yearly volumes reached record levels and premium products gained share reaching ~35% of trade sales, reinforcing higher average realisations. The Company continued its focus on efficiently utilising its capacity while ensuring expansions continued in a structured manner as consolidated capacity reached 109 MTPA and the Company is on track for 119 MTPA by the end of FY 2026-27. Despite a volatile near-term cost environment, the Company's growth trajectory is increasingly supported by the integration of AI and advanced technologies across operations, enabling faster decision-making, improved efficiencies and accelerated infrastructure delivery.
Operational cash flows and internal 
accruals remain the primary sources of funding for expansion and sustainability investments, enabling the Company to strengthen working capital, improve treasury returns and maintain a conservative capital structure. Going forward, Ambuja Cements will continue to fund growth through internal cash generation and selective asset optimisation while preserving strong credit metrics and return-on-capital discipline.
Earnings 
Ambuja Cements delivered a  
sustainable operating performance in FY 2025-26, supported by strong volume growth and a sustained recovery in margins. Revenue from operations stood at H 40,656 crore in FY 2025-26, reflecting financial resilience and scale. The Company achieved volume growth of more than twice the industry average, driven by a focused strategy to strengthen market presence and improve realisations. EBITDA stood 
at H 887 per tonne during the period, benefitting from pricing discipline, premiumisation and effective  
cost control.  
 Net profit rose to H 5,637 crore, underscoring improving operating leverage as volumes scaled. Key initiatives included expanding the share of premium products, intensifying branding campaigns, strengthening influencer engagement through technical teams, delivering region-specific value-added solutions and upgrading physical infrastructure. Looking ahead, continued emphasis on premium and solution-led offerings, supported by disciplined cost optimisation and integration synergies across the cement 
business and the wider Group platform, is expected to drive sustained profitability and  
improved returns.

Integration and Optimisation  
of Acquired Assets
Ambuja Cements has pursued a focused M&A strategy to accelerate scale, secure raw-material, and drive cost leadership. Since joining the Adani portfolio, the Group has added 32.90 MTPA of capacity through strategic acquisitions (inclusive of under construction capacity), at a cumulative transaction value of  H 24,896 crore. Key acquisitions include Orient Cement Limited, Penna Cement Industries, Sanghi Industries, Asian Fine Cements, Asian Concretes & Cements and a grinding unit at Tuticorin.
The integration programme of 
acquired assets was completed in FY 2025-26 and has been centred on operational harmonisation — aligning procurement, logistics, plant operations and commercial processes to realise synergies in freight, clinker optimisation, and energy sourcing. As a result, Ambuja Cements expanded its consolidated capacity to 109 MTPA, reduced lead distances and logistics costs in core markets, and strengthened market share across regions.
Integration has also enabled 
targeted CAPEX and OPEX initiatives (debottlenecking, standardised maintenance, and productivity improvements) that lift asset utilisation and cost efficiencies. These actions, combined with Group advantages in power, coal and ports, accelerate the Company’s pathway to its medium-term capacity and cost targets.
The Company has achieved early 
operational success across the acquired assets. Capacity utilisation has improved meaningfully for acquired assets, at 54%, improved by 16 pp compared to 38% last year. These outcomes reflect disciplined execution of its integration and optimisation playbook.

Leveraging Group Synergies
Ambuja Cements harnesses the strength of the Adani Group’s integrated portfolio to enhance operational efficiency, cost competitiveness and execution certainty across its value chain. By leveraging synergies in mining, energy, logistics, infrastructure and shared centres of excellence, the Company secures reliable access to key inputs, optimises logistics, and benefits from assured project delivery within set timelines and budgets. These synergies support scale-led growth and reinforce operational resilience, foster circular economy solutions and strengthen community engagement, creating sustainable value for stakeholders while also ensuring that the Company is poised to overcome near-term uncertainties.

Property, plant and equipment comprise the majority of non-current assets, aligned with the Company’s expansion roadmap. Maintaining a debt-free balance sheet with robust net worth and liquidity metrics, Ambuja Cements is well-positioned to fund near-term capital expenditure largely through internal accruals and selective Group support. Tax Transparency

Financial Capital
Launch of the ‘Cement Chalisa’
Ambuja Cements launched the 
‘Cement Chalisa’, a compact, structured knowledge pack designed by the Board and CEO to unite stakeholders around the Company’s strategy, operating model and value drivers. Framed around a simple menu - Past, Plants & Projects, Products, People, Prominent Synergy, Profitability & Financials, Principles, Policies and Primary Value Driver, the Chalisa translates the CEO’s ROCE-led vision (RESQ, Reimagination of Business model) into an accessible, repeatable reference for leadership, plant teams, channel partners and investors. The initiative combines practical content (project and plant updates, product positioning and financial highlights) with cultural elements (local language couplets and messaging) to deepen engagement and expedite decision-making. Early usage has made strategic information universally available across functions, improving clarity on priorities, accelerating approvals and strengthening alignment between commercial, operational and sustainability agendas. Ambuja Cements now plans to embed the Cement Chalisa in induction, investor packs and plant-level dashboards, using it as a living document to track milestones and cascade the Company’s strategic narrative across its footprint.
Strengthening Investor Confidence Through Transparency
During the year, Ambuja 
Cements strengthened investor engagement by hosting its inaugural Capital Markets Plant Visit at the Marwar Mundwa Integrated Plant, Rajasthan.  The two-day programme brought together 46 senior analysts from 38 leading domestic and global institutions, providing an immersive view of operations, leadership perspective and strategic priorities. Plant walkthroughs, leadership interactions and portfolio demonstrations highlighted the Company’s transformation into a future-ready building materials solutions provider, with a strong focus on capacity expansion, digital integration and Group synergies. Positive feedback reinforced confidence in execution capability and  long-term growth prospects.
Building on this momentum, 
Adani Cement hosted its second Capital Markets Plant Visit at the Sanghipuram integrated plant in Kutch, Gujarat, welcoming prominent analysts and investors. The visit showcased Sanghipuram’s scale, resource strength and strategic importance, including over one billion tonnes of limestone resources, integrated clinkerisation and grinding operations, and a highly digitised control environment. Discussions also highlighted logistics advantages from a captive jetty and ongoing investments in rail connectivity to enhance multi-modal efficiency. Collectively, these engagements reinforced transparency and strengthened investor confidence in Adani Cement’s capability to overcome near-term challenges and achieve long-term goals.

Raw Material Sourcing
Limestone, clay and laterite are sourced from 
captive and leased mines using responsible mining practices, with a focus on resource efficiency, safety and minimal environmental impact.
Raw Material Preparation  
Extracted materials are crushed, ground and homogenised through automated systems to achieve the required chemical composition for consistent clinker quality.
Clinker Production  
The prepared raw mix is processed in energy-efficient rotary kilns at high temperatures (1,400-1,500°C) to produce clinker, with increasing use of alternative fuels to reduce energy intensity and emissions.
Cement Grinding and Blending   
Clinker is cooled and ground with gypsum and supplementary materials such as fly ash and slag to produce a range of blended and specialised cement products.
Packaging and Storage 
Finished cement is packed in bags or dispatched in bulk and stored in controlled facilities to prevent moisture ingress and preserve product quality.
Logistics 
A multimodal logistics network—road, rail and sea—ensures timely and cost-efficient delivery, supported by digital tracking and route optimisation.
Sales and Technical Assistance   
Strong distributor and contractor networks, focused branding, and on-site technical support help customers optimise product use and strengthen long-term relationships.Manufacturing Highlights

Capacity Expansion
Ambuja Cements made strides to expand its capacity in FY 2025–26. Consolidated cement capacity reached 109 MTPA during the year. It aims achieve its target of 119 MTPA capacity in a structured and phased manner by  FY 2026-27. 
During the year, the Company 
commissioned new grinding capacities across Marwar, Farakka, Sankrail, Sindri, Krishnapatnam, alongside additional clinker units at Jodhpur and Bhatapara. With an aim to increase its capacity to 119 MTPA by FY 2026-27, the Company continues to focus on consciously shifting towards stabilising newly commissioned capacities and improving utilisation across the existing base. Enhancing Efficiency through In-plant Automation
Ambuja Cements introduced in-plant automation to tighten vehicle access, automate weighment and streamline documentation at packing plants. By linking order allocation to gate entry, deploying automatic weighbridges and auto-generated invoices, the Company eliminated manual interventions, reduced weight variances and shortened processing times. CASE STUDY 
Mechanised Raw Material Sampling to Enhance Safety, Accuracy and Efficiency
Ambuja Cements replaced manual, time-consuming and inconsistent raw-material sampling with a mobile, mechanised sampling system at its Marwar Mundwa unit.  
 A hydraulic auger now extracts representative samples directly from wagons and trucks to a fixed sampling point, removing bias and safety risks associated with manual sampling. The solution delivers consistent top-to-bottom samples for materials such as gypsum, china clay and coal, speeds up receipt processes, improves traceability and transparency, and enhances on-site safety and labour efficiency.  
Overall, the mechanised system has reduced sampling time, raised sample reliability and strengthened materials control across inbound supply streams.With an aim to increase its capacity to 119 MTPA by FY 2026-27, the Company's focus is consciously shifting towards stabilising newly commissioned capacities and improving utilisation across the existing base. By prioritising higher utilisation and operating efficiency, the Company is strengthening the ability to meet its overall growth objectives while overcoming near-term hurdles through disciplined execution with further capacity additions being pursued more gradually once optimal utilisation levels are achieved, reflecting disciplined capital allocation and a focus on return on capital employed.

Agnigati: Ambuja Cements’ National Logistics Meet and Digital Logistics Platform
On 19 August 2025, Ambuja Cements convened Agnigati - The National Logistics Meet, a flagship industry gathering that brought together more than 200 transporters, warehousing partners, service providers and logistics leaders to share innovations and align on a greener, more efficient logistics future. The event served as a collaboration forum and a launchpad for Ambuja Cements’ logistics digitalisation agenda, showcasing electric-vehicle pilots, port-linked grinding solutions and best practices for sustainable, high-performance supply chains.
At the heart of Ambuja Cements’ 
logistics transformation is Agnigati—a fully digital, end -to-end 
logistics orchestration platform that is redefining speed, accuracy and transparency across the Company’s supply chain. Agnigati seamlessly integrates trip generation, order allocation and in -plant gate operations 
with real -time delivery -order 
creation, automated invoicing and livestock -transfer management, 
ensuring faster and error -free 
dispatches. The platform enables e-invoice and e -way-bill automation, supports instant document uploads, and generates IGPs and loading advice directly at plant locations. Through deep SAP integration, Agnigati creates a unified data spine that links warehouses, plants and transporters—driving smarter decision-making, tighter controls, and a more responsive logistics ecosystem. Purpose -built for 
scale, Agnigati boosts operational reliability, cuts turnaround times and elevates customer fulfilment—turning logistics into a strategic edge that delivers agility, service excellence and sustainable value.
The combined effect of the 
Agnigati meet and the portal has been threefold: (1) stronger partner alignment through shared visibility and capability building,  (2) measurable operational benefits from process automation and real-time controls, and (3) acceleration of Ambuja Cements’ sustainability agenda by enabling modal shift, EV pilots and more efficient route/source matching. By turning a one-day convening into an ongoing digital collaboration platform, Ambuja Cements has created a scalable logistics operating model that reduces lead times, improves  on-time performance and supports its expanding coastal and depot network.
Navgati: Reimagining Logistics 
When Scale Becomes Strategy
As businesses grow, scale initially 
delivers advantage. Over time, however, scale itself demands a higher order of discipline. Beyond a point, leadership is no longer defined by size, but by how intelligently that size is organised and governed.
Adani Cement has reached this 
inflection point.
With an expanding manufacturing 
footprint and a deepening market presence, the organisation is reimagining logistics through Navgati —a strategic framework 
that marks the next phase of the One Cement  journey. Navgati 
reflects a deliberate shift in the role of logistics: from a movement -led 
support function to a decisive lever of competitiveness, reliability, and value creation.
In this new paradigm, the central 
question is no longer how far the network can reach. It is how precisely, predictably,  and productively  it can serve. 
The future of cement logistics will not be defined by kilometres travelled, but by the intelligence applied to planning, execution, and governance.
Navgati aligns cement sales 
with the natural markets of manufacturing plants, driving improved asset utilisation, shorter lead distances, optimised freight costs, and stronger service reliability. Cost -efficient delivery 
remains non -negotiable, but 
efficiency is pursued alongside productivity, resilience, and long -term value.This shift is embedded through system -led governance  and a 
unified operating framework across the logistics value chain. Digital architecture enables a transition from reactive operations to predictive orchestration, while structural enablers—including DIGIPIN -based freight allocation, 
automation, GPS -enabled visibility, 
centralised S&OP -driven demand 
planning, enhanced rail efficiency, and accelerated EV deployment—strengthen both performance and sustainability.
Supported by a robust backbone 
of GPS -governed trucks, captive 
maritime assets, and multimodal infrastructure, Navgati builds more than efficiency. It builds resilience, enhances agility, and strengthens the confidence to serve a nation building at unprecedented scale and speed.
Through Navgati, integration 
at Adani Cement is not merely structural—it is operational. Not just aligned—but optimised. Executed with discipline, logistics ceases to be a cost to manage and becomes an advantage that compounds over time.

Automated ePOD & Touchless Freight Billing
Ambuja Cements implemented an end-to-end ePOD and touchless freight-billing system to eliminate paper-based processes and manual interventions across logistics billing. Automated validations, real-time delivery confirmation and seamless integration with vendor portals reduced processing time from 15 days to just 1 day, while improving accuracy and transparency.  The initiative delivered annualised cost savings, enabled faster vendor payments, minimised exceptions and strengthened auditability—demonstrating how digitalisation can significantly enhance logistics efficiency and  financial discipline.Cost Efficiency 
Ambuja Cements remains firmly focused on cost leadership through a comprehensive programme of operational and energy efficiency initiatives to overcome the volatile external cost environment. Fuel costs are optimised through higher use of alternative fuels, supported by the installation of chlorine bypass systems and additional shredding infrastructure, alongside strategic sourcing and negotiations. Power costs are reduced through maximisation of renewable energy through Solar and wind projects and the installation and commissioning of Waste Heat Recovery Systems (WHRS) across suitable kiln lines. Thermal energy consumption is further lowered by replacing outdated clinker coolers with high-efficiency systems to improve heat recuperation and reduce fuel usage. Electrical energy intensity is addressed through high-efficiency motors and drives, rigorous process audits, benchmarking and optimisation of grinding and clinkering operations. Productivity gains are reinforced through advanced control systems and digital tools to optimise kiln and mill performance—collectively strengthening the Company’s cost competitiveness and long-term sustainability.Driver Management Centres
Ambuja Cements is strengthening road and logistics safety through a structured, technology-led approach focused on prevention and accountability. Ambuja Cements has established world-class Driver Management Centres (DMCs) across its plants, manned by trained safety professionals to safeguard the  well-being of all associated drivers.  The centres deliver structured defensive driving programmes, GPS-enabled monitoring and behaviour-based safety coaching, complemented by continuous road-safety awareness initiatives and stakeholder engagement.
The DMCs prioritise driver health 
and dignity through regular medical and eye check-ups, provide access to nutritious meals, clean rest areas and hygienic sanitation facilities. By recognising drivers and their families as essential partners in the value chain, Ambuja Cements reinforces its commitment to safer roads, improved livelihoods and responsible, inclusive growth.
The Company's Driver Management 
Centre (DMC) network currently covers 36 sites and 62 counsellors for wider coverage. A Logistics Safety Dashboard tracks key driving risks such as over-speeding, harsh braking/acceleration, and fatigue indicators, enabling targeted counselling and corrective action. To drive ownership, a Logistics Safety Scorecard recognises top-performing drivers, transporters, sites, and regions based on safety KPIs and compliance. Going forward, Ambuja Cements plans to strengthen recognition programmes, introduce mobile-based monitoring, install dashcams, and implement automated vehicle fitness checks at gate entry to further advance its Zero Harm ambition.

CASE STUDY 
Ambuja Cements implemented an Internet of Things (IoT) sensor programme at its Marwar Mundwa unit to shift from reactive to predictive maintenance and reduce unplanned equipment downtime. A total of 1,667 sensors were installed to enable real-time monitoring of critical parameters such as vibration, temperature, sound and triaxial movement, with instant alerts and periodic analytics accessible to site engineers. This data-driven approach addressed earlier challenges of limited asset visibility, delayed diagnostics and unexpected breakdowns. The initiative delivered tangible results, including prevention of critical air-slide blower failures, saving approximately 40 hours of downtime, improvement in cooler fan efficiency through corrective balancing and alignment, and early detection of a gearbox bearing fault in a chain conveyor. Overall, the IoT rollout enhanced asset reliability, improved maintenance responsiveness, reduced operating costs and strengthened operational efficiency through faster, informed decision-making.

Drone Monitoring for Safe Operations 
The Company continues to 
ensure manufacturing excellence by deploying advanced drone technology to enhance efficiency, safety and asset reliability. Drones are used across multiple plant functions, including ultrasonic thickness measurement of chimneys and ducts, inspection of welding and bolting in preheaters, conveyor structures and clinker silo domes, and thermal imaging of cyclones and other high-temperature zones. They also enable accurate volumetric assessment of covered and uncovered stockpiles. From a safety perspective, drones support PPE compliance checks, monitoring of critical shutdown activities, housekeeping audits, mine mapping and contouring, security surveillance, confined-space inspections in cyclones, silos, kilns and chimneys, as well as internal and external area surveys and truck movement monitoring—significantly reducing exposure to high-risk tasks.

CASE STUDY 
Overcoming Groundwater Challenges with Premium Products  
At a major commercial 
complex project in Tenali, Andhra Pradesh, Ambuja Kawach proved its strength in overcoming severe ground and moisture challenges, securing a decisive product conversion. The site was characterised by a high groundwater table and expansive black cotton soil, leading to persistent seepage and waterlogging in the cellar area—conditions that posed risks to durability and structural integrity.Recognising the need for a specialised solution, the TS field team and Dealer collaborated closely with the contractor, structural consultant to recommend Ambuja Kawach for its superior compressive strength, enhanced water-repellent properties and ability to produce denser, more durable concrete. Through on-site testing and structured application guidance, the product was deployed strategically to arrest capillary action and strengthen foundational elements. Continuous technical supervision and integrated planning ensured smooth execution of the foundation work despite challenging conditions. The performance of Ambuja Kawach reinforc ed client’s confidence, 
validating its positioning as a premium solution for moisture-prone and water-sensitive environments.

a busy educational facility.

Accelerated Digitalisation 
Ambuja Cements has accelerated its digital transformation, embedding intelligence across operations to enhance reliability, cut costs and fast-track decision-making. The Company’s Cement Intelligent Network Operations Centre (CiNOC) and the Adani–Ambuja AI-first platform provide a centralised,  
AI-enabled control layer that unifies ERP, IoT, fleet telematics and analytics. These foundations support real-time plant monitoring, predictive maintenance, remote substation operation, digital sales portals and paper-less logistics (ePOD), while pilot deployments of agentic AI and project-to-operations digital twins are being used to optimise dispatch, maintenance and energy use.
The programme is pragmatic and 
outcomes driven. Dealer onboarding time has fallen from a week to under 30 minutes; an autonomous invoice-to-pay pilot has cut errors by 90% and reduced manual effort by 80%; and logistics turnaround at 17 plants has improved by roughly 25%. Complementary initiatives including advanced fleet management with near-complete GPS coverage, AI-enabled tracking, automated planning and a standardised ERP backbone have delivered faster invoice processing, lower document costs and improved route discipline.

Electrical Energy Forecasting and Scheduling Optimisation 
Ambuja Cements implemented a 
live electrical energy forecasting and scheduling optimisation solution to strengthen power management across its plants.  By integrating real-time reporting with the Real-Time Data Integration (RDT) framework and the AE&L application, the initiative centralised power consumption data, enabling accurate forecasting, intelligent scheduling, and proactive load management. The system significantly reduced manual intervention, improved decision-making speed through automated alerts, and optimised energy usage to minimise wastage. As a result, Ambuja Cements enhanced operational efficiency, reduced energy-related costs, improved resource utilisation, and reinforced its commitment to sustainable and efficient manufacturing operations  across locations.
Redefining Cement Logistics through Digital Innovation: DIGIPIN 
Taking logistics excellence a step further, Ambuja Cements became the first in India to adopt DIGIPIN, the Government of India’s Digital Address System, which divides the country into precise 4 m x 4 m grids, each assigned a unique 10-character alphanumeric code.This innovation enables pinpoint accuracy in identifying delivery locations, significantly enhancing transparency, traceability and accountability across the distribution network. Supported by AI-led planning, dynamic forecasting, ePOD systems and a strategic modal shift from road to rail and sea—reducing CO
2 
emissions by up to 60%—the Company has achieved tangible outcomes, including a 23% reduction in route deviations,  
30% faster invoicing, and improved delivery timelines with higher dispatch accuracy.Logistics Transformation 
At Ambuja Cements, logistics is treated as a critical extension of quality—where precision, purpose and progress travel with every consignment. Recognising that quality does not end at the plant gate, the Company has built one of India’s most advanced cement logistics networks, comprising 60,000+ GPS-enabled trucks, 11 GPWIS rakes,  
17 sea-based terminals including 10 bulk cement terminals, all designed to deliver smarter, cleaner and faster outcomes at scale. This robust backbone ensures that every kilometre, delivery and movement is engineered for reliability and efficiency.
Complementing technology with 
people-centric practices, Ambuja Cements continues to invest in Driver Management Centres, prioritising safety, training and well-being for its frontline logistics workforce. Together, these initiatives reinforce a simple but powerful belief: at Ambuja Cements, quality lives in every logistical move—every truck dispatched, every destination mapped and every delivery fulfilled with precision and purpose.

Management System 
Ambuja Cements’ performance management system is designed to strengthen execution, encourage innovation, and enable high-quality collaboration across teams.  
The Company follows a structured goal-setting approach based on SMART principles (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound), ensuring that individual priorities remain aligned with organisational objectives. Goals are further translated into clear milestones through team involvement and periodic tracking, helping drive accountability and sustained performance. Continuous feedback is embedded into the process through half yearly and annual reviews and 360-degree feedback mechanisms, promoting transparency, trust and continuous improvement. Performance check-ins serve as critical progress reviews, enabling timely course correction and ensuring consistent delivery  against targets.Performance Appraisal 
Ambuja Cements’ performance appraisal process includes performance measurement, rating, promotion recommendations, and individual feedback. Outcomes from the appraisal process support decisions related to rewards, 
recognition, promotions and career progression. All eligible employees, including permanent workers, undergo annual appraisal, while performance evaluations for non-permanent workers are conducted by contractors in line with defined terms and conditions.
The Company recorded a significant 
number of promotions during the year. This reflects a strong emphasis on internal career progression, merit-based advancement and structured performance evaluation and succession planning across functions and locations.Diversity, Equity

Human Capital
Gender Diversity: Structural Context, Sectoral & Technical Workforce Realities and 
Sustainable Transition
Gender diversity remains a 
strategic priority and is governed through leadership oversight and ESG frameworks at both Group and business levels. Workforce composition and gender representation are reviewed periodically, with interventions calibrated to business models, role requirements, and operating contexts.
India presents a unique structural 
paradox. Women constitute approximately 42–43% of India’s STEM graduates, one of the highest proportions globally. However, this strong educational pipeline does not translate proportionately into technical and operational roles. The gap is not one of capability or qualification, but of structural, geographic, and sector -specific constraints. The 
location of cement plants are characterised by geographically dispersed and remote project locations, continuous on -site 
presence requirements, rotational or extended work schedules, and high mobility demands. Despite a robust supply of technically qualified women at the national level, many are unwilling or unable to pursue long -term careers in 
remote project locations due to safety concerns, limited access to suitable housing and sanitation infrastructure, mobility constraints, family responsibilities, and social factors.
Management Approach and 
Transition Path
Recognising these realities, the 
Adani Portfolio has adopted a calibrated and phased approach to advancing gender diversity, focusing on sustainable integration rather than short -term 
numerical optimisation.
In the near term, efforts are 
concentrated on improving representation in functions where the external talent pool is relatively deeper and geographic constraints are lower, including corporate roles, HR, GCC, Project planning & Monitoring Group, Techno-Commercial, Finance, Digital, Sustainability, and Emerging technology domains.In parallel, long -term 
interventions are directed at addressing the technical workforce gap through sustainable initiatives like:
Partnerships with ITIs, 
polytechnics, and skilling institutions to build industry -aligned technical 
capabilities among women.
Progressive deployment of 
automation and digital systems that reduce physical intensity and enable broader participation wherever feasible.
Structured retention and 
progression mechanisms, including mentorship, transparent career pathways, and bias-resistant systems.
Way Forward
Gender diversity outcomes across 
the Group and Cement Business reflect both current labour market constraints and deliberate management choices aligned to operational realities. Progress is expected to be deliberate and phased.

Adani Cement Cricket League – Building Premium Performance Through People
The launch of the Adani Cement Cricket League marked a first in the Company’s history, transforming a sporting initiative into a powerful platform for collaboration, inclusion and shared purpose. Human Rights
Ambuja Cements upholds 
fundamental human rights as an integral part of its values and corporate responsibility. The Company’s Human Rights Policy is aligned with internationally recognised framework. Safety Cs, including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work, and the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights. Applicable to employees, associates, customers, vendors and contractors, the policy outlines Ambuja Cements’ commitment to respecting and safeguarding human rights across its operations and value chain.
To strengthen awareness and 
accountability, 100% of employees were trained on human rights during the reporting period. Recognising that business operations and supply chain practices can influence human rights outcomes, the Company enforces a Supplier Code of Conduct for all suppliers. The Code reflects zero tolerance for child labour and forced labour and reinforces expectations on fair wages, reasonable working hours, occupational health and safety, prevention of human trafficking, non-discrimination, and respect for freedom of association and collective bargaining.
Ambuja Cements fosters a 
workplace culture that protects dignity, privacy and individual safety, while ensuring a discrimination-free environment. The Company’s Policy on Freedom of Association supports these principles, and in FY 2025–26, 100% of site-based workers were members of trade unions. Additionally, the Employee Grievance Redressal Policy provides a structured channel for raising concerns, including anonymous reporting, ensuring confidentiality and fair resolution.

#2
At Ambuja Cements' Rabriyawas 
unit, resilience during a critical shutdown was driven by strong leadership accountability and disciplined safety governance. Safety as a Business Enabler 
#1
At Ambuja Cements, Safety is integral to operational excellence and business resilience. Availability of Silo plays a essential role for sustainable operations and requires strong & robust governance. Silo cleaning is a high risk operation and requires competent silo cleaning champions and competent contractors. The Silo cleaning workshop was conducted which certifies 43 silo cleaning champions across the sites. Silo cleaning was completed under the supervision of these Silo cleaning champions with robust technological intervention like Use of BinWhip machine, Use of Cardox and use of drones resulted in achieving Zero harm in 30 nos’ of Silo cleaning and reliable operation.
#3
Bhatapara is an integral unit for the Company as it services the eastern market of the country. During the year, an unexpected failure in the WHRS duct structure was transformed effectively. With no injuries reported, immediate evacuation, isolation and emergency protocols were enforced under strong leadership accountability. A structured risk assessment, detailed method statement and tandem lifting strategy using cranes were implemented following cross-functional planning sessions. Continuous supervision, certified equipment and rigorous safety controls ensured disciplined execution. Within a short span of days, the duct was safely lowered without incident, transforming a high-risk situation into a benchmark example of safety-first leadership, collaboration and operational resilience led by good governance and management support.With unified efforts across all plants, the Company’s Silo champions have turned safety into a true

CASE STUDY 
Suraksha Bandhan: Turning Tradition into a Safety Movement   
In August 2025, Adani Cement reimagined Suraksha Bandhan as a powerful safety-led campaign that brought together people across its operations and communities under one shared promise—care and protection for all. More than 1,02,700 individuals across 192 locations  
spanning plants, project sites, RMX units, sales offices, mines and logistics hubs participated by tying a specially designed Suraksha Band on their wrists. More than a symbolic thread, it became a visible pledge to uphold safety, look out for one another, and strengthen a culture of collective responsibility. The initiative stood out for being leadership-led and people-driven, creating a strong chain of accountability from senior leaders to frontline teams. Its impact extended beyond the workplace, reaching colonies and schools, with 22,000+ children joining the movement—reinforcing that safety is not limited to worksites, but a way of life.  
By blending emotion with purpose, Suraksha Bandhan evolved into a lasting cultural marker for Adani Cement—deepening unity, raising awareness, and embedding the spirit of #WeCare across every level of the organisation.

Climate Governance
Climate governance at the Company 
follows a three-level structure. At the highest level is the Corporate Responsibility Committee (CRC), made up of Independent Directors, which oversees sustainability and climate strategies, initiatives, and reviews key performance indicators (KPIs) each quarter. The second level consists of senior management (MANCOM), led by the CEO and CFO, who are responsible for integrating the broader sustainability and climate strategies with overall business strategy. The third level is the ESG team, headed by the Chief Sustainability Officer, which implements the ESG strategy, prioritises material topics, monitors KPI performance across the business, and ensures alignment with both global and national expectations as well as those of other stakeholders. In addition, the Risk Management Committee (RMC) oversees sustainability and ESG-related risks. Climate risks are now central to the Company's enterprise risk management process.
Environmental Policy and 
Management System 
Ambuja Cements’ Environmental 
Management System provides a structured framework to ad-vance sustainability across all operations. It aligns company policies and procedures with  industry best practices and standards, enabling proactive identification and management of climate risks, targeted action on waste minimisation, and stronger resource efficiency through recycling and reuse. The Company also promotes alignment of its environmental actions with national and global climate priorities, underscoring its broader commitment to sustainable development. These policies are implemented across all sites and are overseen by the Corporate Responsibility Committee (CRC), consisting of Independent Directors and reports to the Board, en-suring strategic oversight and accountability.

Improving Energy Efficiency
Ambuja Cements is consistently 
working to reduce both thermal and electrical energy consumption per tonne of product. Several of its facilities are engaged in India’s Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme, which has led to a continuous decline in specific thermal energy consumption over time. Under the PAT programme, industries identified as high-energy consumers are required to submit annual energy consumption reports and undergo mandatory energy audits. The scheme establishes energy consumption benchmarks, verifies savings through Energy Saving Certificates (Ecerts), and enables the trading of these certificates. This initiative has effectively reduced energy usage and carbon emissions, thereby supporting the advancement of more sustainable operations.Specific Thermal Energy

Co-processing of Waste
The cement industry is 
characterised by high energy consumption, with emissions from fossil fuels constituting a significant source of carbon output in this sector. Ambuja Cements addresses this challenge through the adoption of advanced co-processing technologies. The Company’s facilities, located throughout India, are equipped with dedicated storage areas, feeding systems, and laboratories to ensure efficient operations. Pre-processing units play a vital role in transforming diverse waste streams—originating from agricultural, municipal, and industrial sources—into a homogenised mixture. This process facilitates the effective feeding of alternative fuels into kilns, thereby reducing dependency on conventional fossil fuels.
Initiatives through Geoclean to 
co-process wastes are closely aligned with the Company’s broader sustainability strategy and carbon reduction goals. By integrating alternative fuels into the Company’s fuel mix, it not only prevents wastes from ending up in landfills and causing environmental harm, but also advances circular economy principles, reduce carbon footprint and enhance fuel flexibility.

plants to improve both thermal and electrical energy efficiency.Thermal Substitution Rate  
(Co-processing Rate)
The Thermal Substitution Rate (TSR) refers to the proportion of heating value from fossil fuels replaced by alternative fuels such as biomass, municipal waste, and industrial waste. These alternative sources possess a high calorific value, enabling them to effectively substitute conventional fossil fuels, including coal and pet coke. An increased TSR contributes to lowering carbon emissions and promotes the principles of a circular economy. Ambuja Cements has set a target to achieve a 23% TSR by 2030, underscoring its dedication to sustainable manufacturing practices.
Optimising Clinker Factor
Clinker is the most carbon intensive component in cement production. The Company is focused on manufacturing blended cement with reduced clinker content by integrating supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) such as fly ash and slag. Through continuous innovation in raw mix design and increased use of SCMs, Ambuja Cements has been able to achieve a clinker factor which is lower than the industry average. This significantly lowers CO
2 emissions per tonne of 
cement. The Company is investing in research and development to further reduce the clinker factor while maintaining the high performance and reliability of the products.
Use of Supplementary 
Cementitious Material
Supplementary Cementitious 
Materials (SCMs) play a vital role in the Company’s commitment to sustainable cement production. The Company utilises substances such as fly ash, slag, calcined clay, and waste gypsum in cement manufacturing, allowing it to partially substitute mined raw materials in products like PPC and PSC. To maximise the benefits of SCMs, the Company selects and proportions these materials with care, considering their chemical and physical properties as well as the required performance standards. Through advanced testing methods and blending technologies, it ensures SCMs are highly reactive, finely ground, and free from any harmful contaminants.
Incorporating SCMs not only drives 
its decarbonisation initiatives but also supports a circular economy by recycling industrial byproducts that would otherwise be disposed of in landfills.

Zero Carbon Heating Technology 
Adani Cement and Coolbrook 
have entered into an agreement for the world’s first commercial deployment of the revolutionary RotoDynamic Heater™ (RDH™) technology to advance cement decarbonisation. This marks the first industrial scale deployment of Coolbrook’s RDH™ technology at one of the plants, advancing Adani Cement’s net-zero goals achievement by 2050 (validated by the SBTi). This technology will decarbonise the calcination phase - the most fossil fuel-intensive stage of cement production. By providing clean heat to dry and enhance the heating value of alternative fuels, the technology enables a significantly higher substitution of fossil fuels with sustainable alternatives. Critically, the RDH™ system will be powered entirely by Adani Cement’s large-scale renewable energy portfolio, ensuring that the industrial heat generated is completely emission free. This deployment demonstrates the real-world feasibility of clean, electrified industrial heat powered entirely by renewables. This positions Adani Cement to spearhead India’s emergence as the world’s clean manufacturing cement hub.
By integrating such cutting-edge 
electrification solutions into the Company’s cement production, Ambuja Cements is accelerating the shift away from fossil fuels, reducing emissions at scale, enhancing the utilisation of clean energy sources, and setting a new standard for low-carbon cement manufacturing. This partnership reflects the Company’s commitment to climate leadership and delivering long-term value through innovation and sustainability.
Ambuja Cements is committed to 
managing air emissions proactively by adhering to regulatory norms and minimising ecological impact. A wide range of advanced air pollution control systems are implemented across plants, and these include:
 yElectrostatic Precipitators (ESP) and bag filters effectively capture particulate matter. yEnclosed conveyor systems help minimise dust release during material movement.
 yDust suppression techniques, such as water spraying on haul roads and stockpiles, reduce airborne particles.
 yCovered transport of raw materials and finished products prevents fugitive dust emissions.
 yGreen belt development around plant perimeters acts as a natural barrier to dust and noise pollution.
All of the Company’s plants are equipped with Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS) that provide real-time data on key pollutants:
 yNitrogen Oxides (NOx)
 ySulphur Oxides (SOx)
 yParticulate Matter (PM)
 yOther significant air pollutantsUse of Technology

Responsible Water Stewardship in Water-Stressed Regions
Two of Ambuja’s manufacturing 
units, Marwar Mundwa, Rabriyawas, are situated in regions identified as water-stressed by the Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA), where responsible and efficient water management is of paramount importance.  These plants consume 14% of the organisation’s total water consumption. Despite geographic challenges, the Company consistently meets all regulatory requirements while implementing proactive measures to minimise its dependence on freshwater sources. 
Through extensive rainwater 
harvesting, along with robust recycling and reuse initiatives, Ambuja Cements ensures sustainable operations and strengthens the preservation of local water ecosystems. 
As a result of the initiatives, 
Marwar Mundwa is 3.1 times water positive and Rabariyawas is 13.9 times water positive.

CASE STUDY 
Water Stewardship Creating Shared Prosperity  
At Ambuja Cements’ Rabriyawas 
plant in Rajasthan, proactive water conservation and management led to the plant achieving a 13.9 water positive status, replenishing significantly more water than it consumes each year. Central to this achievement is the creation of 49 farm ponds across neighbouring villages, adding 2.22 lakh cubic metres of rainwater storage in the current year. These ponds have alleviated water scarcity and now support irrigation across 150–170 acres during the Rabi season, enabling multi-cropping in both Rabi and Zaid cycles. As a result, farming households have recorded a 35–40% increase in incomes. Local farmers, including Shobha Devi Prajapat, describe the initiative as transformative, enabling year-round cultivation and strengthening economic resilience.
Ambuja Cements is committed to sustainable resource consumption, minimising waste generation and advancing circular economy principles across its operations. The Company goes beyond regulatory requirements to ensure safe, compliant, and responsible waste handling. Waste minimisation and recycling are integral to Ambuja Cements’ sustainability strategy, with a strong focus on maximising the use of waste-derived resources to reduce dependence on mined materials and avoid environmentally harmful disposal. Regular waste audits are conducted to identify improvement areas and implement targeted reduction actions. With ambitious targets and continuous investments, the Company maintains zero waste to landfill and strengthens employee awareness through regular training programmes, reinforcing a culture of environmental stewardship.

Ambuja Cements becomes First Indian Cement Company to Adopt TNFD recommendations
In a landmark step towards nature-
positive growth, Adani Cement—comprising Ambuja Cements Limited and its subsidiaries—became the first company in the Indian cement industry to adopt the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) recommendations, joining a select group of global leaders driving sustainable manufacturing and responsible construction. As the world’s ninth-largest building materials solutions provider and part of the diversified Adani portfolio, the Company’s adoption of TNFD further reinforces its commitment to embedding nature-positive principles into long-term business strategy and operational decision-making.  This milestone reinforces the Company’s commitment to systematically identify, assess, manage and disclose nature-related risks and opportunities, with TNFD-aligned formal disclosures set to begin from FY 2025-26. 
The adoption builds on Adani 
Cement’s existing nature risk assessment and disclosure practices aligned with globally recognised frameworks and strengthens its broader ESG strategy aimed at supporting India’s climate and nature ambitions. The initiative also complements the Company’s ongoing decarbonisation efforts, including the world’s first commercial deployment of Coolbrook’s RotoDynamic Heater™ technology, further advancing its journey towards climate leadership and sustainable industrial transformation.
Backed by strong on-ground action, 
the Company has already advanced large-scale afforestation with over 2.25 million trees planted, achieved 12x water positivity, and implemented biodiversity conservation efforts across its operations. With a portfolio comprising majorly of blended cement, Adani Cement is integrating responsible resource management into business decision-making—setting a new benchmark for transparency, accountability and environmental stewardship in India’s cement sector.
CASE STUDY 
Geoclean – Protecting Brands, Preserving the Planet  
Adani Cement’s sustainable waste management arm, Geoclean, partnered with a leading FMCG companies to pioneer a responsible solution for market return waste—products that do not reach consumers and require secure end-of-life handling. Under this partnership, trade rejects such as juices and honey are prevented from leaking into grey markets or reaching landfills.  
It helps to safeguard consumer safety and brand trust. Market returns are securely channelled through a controlled system and co-processed at authorised Geoclean facilities, ensuring 100% brand protection and responsible disposal. The initiative has delivered measurable outcomes at scale, with 15,000+ tonnes of market returns diverted and operations remaining 100% landfill-free, reinforcing how business can act as a catalyst for circularity while reducing environmental contamination and landfill burden.
Biodiversity management is a key focus area in the Company’s materiality assessment, recognising that healthy ecosystems help mitigate natural disasters and provide critical ecological services that support businesses and society. The Company’s biodiversity policy guides the identification and evaluation of nature-related risks across project sites and applies a mitigation hierarchy of avoid, minimise, restore and offset, with progress tracked regularly. The policy extends across operations as well as suppliers and value chain partners. It aims to achieve No Net Deforestation through time-bound afforestation programmes, deliver No Net Loss of Biodiversity across operations (including sites near critical habitats), and progress towards an ultimate goal of  
Net Positive Gain.
To strengthen its approach, 
Ambuja Cements conducted a comprehensive Nature Risk Assessment, including a Biodiversity Risk Assessment, aligned with the TNFD LEAP methodology. This enables the Company to identify and disclose nature-related dependencies (such as reliable access to clean water) and impacts—both positive and negative—on ecosystems.  
These dependencies and impacts may create physical risks (acute or chronic, driven by climate events, geological factors or ecosystem shifts such as soil degradation) and transition risks linked to evolving regulatory and policy expectations. At the same time, the Company also recognises nature-related opportunities that support restoration, reduce impacts and create value for both ecosystems and business resilience.

Biodiversity Risk Assessment
As a cement manufacturer, the 
Company has a direct and material dependence on natural capital, particularly through raw material extraction and water use, while also relying indirectly on ecosystem services that regulate climate, water cycles and protection from natural hazards. Recognising that mining and land-use changes can affect biodiversity and ecosystem resilience, the Company undertook a comprehensive Nature Risk Assessment, including a Biodiversity Risk Assessment, for all its sites except for Penna and Sanghi sites which recently got merged with Ambuja, and 10 km distance around the site, to better understand these dependencies and impacts.
The assessment was conducted 
using the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) LEAP approach, a globally recognised framework that enabled the Company to map interactions with nature, evaluate dependencies and impacts, and identify nature-related risks and opportunities. These risks span physical, transition and systemic categories, ranging from extreme weather and ecosystem degradation to regulatory shifts and large-scale ecological change.Biodiversity Action Plan
In response to identified risks, 
Ambuja Cements developed a comprehensive Biodiversity Action Plan (BAP) aligned with the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Mitigation Hierarchy and built around nature-based solutions. 
The BAP includes site-specific 
actions such as greenbelt development, wildlife monitoring, rainwater harvesting structures, and mangrove restoration initiatives, reinforcing the Company’s commitment to managing biodiversity risks while strengthening long-term ecological sustainability.Biodiversity Mitigation Hierarchy
